Most redesigns go one of two bad ways: the site looks better but converts the same, or it launches and the rankings vanish overnight. We do neither. How do I redesign my website without losing SEO and traffic?

You protect SEO during a redesign by keeping your URL structure (or mapping 301 redirects for every changed page), preserving your existing content and metadata, migrating your schema, and testing everything on staging before launch. Done right, a redesign keeps your rankings and improves them, because the new site is faster, mobile-first, and better structured than the old one.

The Chandler-East Valley market

Why ranking in Chandler is a moving target

Chandler is the heart of Arizona's "Silicon Desert" — Intel runs its largest U.S. manufacturing campus here at Ocotillo, now expanding with the massive Fab 52/62 buildout, and Microchip, NXP, and a deep semiconductor cluster sit alongside it. That means thousands of high-income, highly educated engineers and tech professionals own homes here, and they research contractors meticulously before they call. Two things shape demand. First, this is the Sonoran Desert, where summer runs 110–115°F for months — when an AC system dies in July, it's a medical emergency, and HVAC and pool-equipment searches dominate. Second, the North American monsoon rolls in July through September with violent dust storms, microbursts, and flash flooding that batter roofs and AC units overnight. Add strict HOA exterior standards across nearly every neighborhood, and Chandler homeowners want a contractor who looks established, responds fast, and clearly knows the East Valley.

When a Chandler AC system dies at 114°F, the contractor already ranking is the one who gets the call.

The real problem

Signs your Chandler site is overdue for a redesign

01

It looks dated and costs you trust

For a high-ticket job, Chandler homeowners — many of them engineers and tech professionals — judge you by your site in seconds. An old, cluttered design quietly sends them to a competitor who looks more established, even when your work is better.

02

It's slow and hard to use on a phone

If your site is clunky or slow on mobile, you're losing the majority of your Chandler visitors before they ever see your offer. A redesign built mobile-first wins them back.

03

It can't keep up when demand surges

Traffic that doesn't turn into calls is wasted — and an old site that gets slow under a peak-heat or monsoon surge loses leads at the exact moment they're worth the most. We rebuild for conversions and for the days your phone should be ringing off the hook.

Chandler Website Redesign FAQ

Questions Chandler owners ask us

How much does a website redesign cost in Chandler?

Most redesigns with us run $2,500 to $9,000 as a one-time project, depending on size and integrations. Fixed price, no surprises, and you own the result.

Will I lose my Google rankings if I redesign?

Not if it's done carefully, and that's exactly how we work. We map 301 redirects for every changed URL, preserve content and metadata, migrate your schema, and test on staging first. Done right, a redesign holds your rankings and usually improves them.

How long does a redesign take?

A focused redesign takes about 3 to 5 weeks; a larger rebuild takes 5 to 9. You get a firm timeline up front and updates at each stage.

How do I know I need a redesign?

If your site is slow on phones, looks dated, is hard to update, isn't bringing in leads, or buckles when peak-heat or monsoon traffic surges, it's costing you work. The free audit tells you plainly whether a redesign is worth it.

Do you migrate my existing content?

Yes. We carry over and improve your existing content, preserve what's ranking, and handle the technical migration so nothing important gets lost.

Will the new site handle peak-heat and monsoon traffic?

Yes, and in Chandler that's a real consideration. When summer peaks or a monsoon storm hits, contractor sites take a surge of traffic, and the slow ones lose leads. We rebuild for speed and keep the call to action obvious so the site converts when demand peaks.

Will the new site be mobile-friendly and fast?

Yes. We rebuild mobile-first and tune for fast load and Core Web Vitals, which lifts both conversions and rankings.

Do I own the redesigned site?

Completely — the site, the domain, and the content. No platform lock-in.

Am I locked into a contract?

No. The redesign is a one-time project. Any ongoing maintenance or SEO is month-to-month.

What's in the free redesign audit?

A clear read on what your current site is costing you in leads and rankings, what the redesign should fix, and a fixed-price quote with a timeline and a safe migration plan.
